question: Do docs/v3's descriptions of cited papers say what the papers say?
method: Ranking: cite/units.py-style scan of docs/v3 Markdown outside code fences and non-bibliography reference lists. A sentence, list item or table row counts as a descriptive unit for an arXiv ID when it contains the ID (or sits in a paragraph that cites only that ID) and states a method, result, number, taxonomy or claim. 167 arXiv works have descriptive units; the ranking only sees arXiv IDs, and it undercounts works described at length under a single 'Primary source' header.

Checking: for the 46 top-ranked works, the full text was fetched from arxiv.org/html (latest version; v1 abstracts where the docs quoted v1 figures) and every descriptive unit was compared with the abstract, introduction, method and results sections, by reading and by searching for each claimed number and term.

Verdicts: 'supported' when every claim matches the paper (loose paraphrase allowed); 'corrected' when at least one claim is not in the paper or contradicts it, and the docs were rewritten with section references or the claim was marked as Roko's own; 'removed' when nothing correct could replace it (none). Severity 'major' means an invented finding, number, mechanism, quotation or a result credited to the wrong paper; 'minor' means a dropped qualifier ('up to'), an overstated genre (a position paper as validation), a wrong affiliation or a misapplied number.
Wrong author labels found on the way were fixed in the same sentences but do not count toward the verdicts.

Regression guard: the phrases removed are now 'prose' entries in citation_errata.json (6 new works, 19 extended), so check_citation_errata.py --prose fails if they return in a section that cites the work.

not_described.note: ranked only because of a version suffix; docs/v3 gives bibliographic entries with no description

recommendation.choice: banner now, cut unchecked numbers to bare citations, and keep checking only the works the docs use as evidence
recommendation.why: 62% of the 45 checked works had at least one unsupported claim and 36% had a major one (an invented finding, number, mechanism or quotation, or another paper's result). Every work read in full in earlier items was also wrong. Errors do not thin out down the ranking, so the unchecked 121 works and the non-arXiv citations should be assumed to carry similar rates. A full check costs about three tool calls per work.
steps: Add a banner to REFERENCES.md and depth/39-references/*: descriptions are unverified unless the work is listed in tools/docs_integrity/content_audit.json.

Cut 'Brief annotation' lines and other one-line descriptions of unchecked works down to the bare citation plus at most a quoted abstract sentence; drop numbers that no one has checked. This is mechanical and scriptable from units.json.

Continue full checks only where the docs cite a work as evidence for a Roko design decision ('validates', 'grounds', 'demonstrates that'), starting with the next 20 by rank and the depth files that name a 'Primary source'.
Keep Roko's own synthesis visibly labelled ('Roko's mapping', 'Roko's own choice'); most major errors were Roko's design rationale written as if a paper had found it.

annotation_cut.rule: Every cited work not listed here (works + summary.earlier_full_reads) lost its annotation in the reference lists: the citation (authors, year, title, venue, identifier) stays, the description and its numbers go. Venue and award notes and '(See NN.)' cross-references were kept. A work counts as checked when its arXiv ID is in this file or, without an ID, when its title or name matches. Script: cut.py (gap-1f72ac scratch), three formats.

chapter_reference_sections.files: list items under Reference/Citation/Sources/Bibliography headings in docs/v3 and docs/v1
chapter_reference_sections.note: left_as_is items carry no annotation the script recognises: most are bare; label-first forms such as '**Author Year** -- Title (Venue)' were not touched

annotation_cut.not_cut: Descriptions in chapter prose (outside reference lists) were not cut; the REFERENCES.md banner says they are unchecked.

works.title: TiMem: Temporal-Hierarchical Memory Consolidation for Long-Horizon Conversational Agents
works.paper_says: Temporal Memory Tree consolidates raw observations into progressively abstracted representations (abstract).

works.title: Phasor Agents: Oscillatory Graphs with Three-Factor Plasticity and Sleep-Staged Learning
unsupported_claims: 'validates the NREM/REM distinction -- NREM for faithful replay and pattern extraction, REM for creative recombination and schema testing'
works.paper_says: Deep-sleep-like phases commit tagged updates in gated write windows; REM-like replay reconstructs and perturbs experience for planning; modes are algorithmic, not physiological (abstract).

works.title: The Missing Knowledge Layer in Cognitive Architectures for AI Agents
works.paper_says: Proposes a Knowledge/Memory/Wisdom/Intelligence decomposition with distinct persistence semantics (abstract).

works.title: Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents
works.paper_says: A learned offline consolidator inspired by complementary learning systems theory (abstract).

works.title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
works.paper_says: A sleep paradigm that distils short-term memories into long-term parameters (Knowledge Seeding) plus dreaming (abstract).

works.title: Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
unsupported_claims: 'identify three categories: stale reads, write contention, memory bloat': the paper lists four other failure modes
'the paper validates these design choices with empirical measurements': it measures one production service, not Roko's design
credited to 'Zhou et al.' (first author Margalit)
works.paper_says: Four failure modes: unauthorized leakage, stale propagation, contradiction persistence, provenance collapse; MemClaw measured without baselines (abstract).

works.title: VIGIL: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specifications in AI Agent Skills
works.paper_says: Runtime enforcement of skill specifications as finite-trace temporal safety properties decided by SMT (§3).

works.title: LLM Agents Are Latent Context Managers: Eliciting Self-Managed Context via State Proprioception
works.paper_says: VISTA's context dashboard ('proprioceptive' is the paper's term) lifts Gemini-3-Flash from 22.7% to 50.7% on LOCA-Bench (abstract).

works.title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation
unsupported_claims: 'continuous verification scores enable accurate capability assessment at 15% of the compute cost': wrong mechanism and number
works.paper_says: A small selected subset of non-agentic instances predicts agentic benchmark scores at under 1/100 of the cost of a full evaluation (§1, Fig. 1).

works.title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation
works.paper_says: Counterfactual rescoring shows strict all-pass scoring in multi-verifier tasks can change agent rankings (abstract).
